## Natural history notes

A tiny seed bug characterized by a narrow oval body, dark brown to black coloration, and fine hairs on the legs and body that give it the “hirtipes” or hairy-legged appearance. In Florida, Cnemodus hirtipes is known from the state and has been recorded in fallen pine cones and bunchgrasses, so it is most likely encountered in pine flatwoods, sandhills, open pinewoods, and grassy forest-edge habitats with dry plant litter. Like other rhyparochromid seed bugs, it feeds mainly on fallen seeds and plant material on or near the ground, helping recycle small plant resources while serving as prey for spiders, ants, birds, and other insect predators.
